previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for recurrent dysphagia and throat pain. She reported food sticking and odynophagia, with no recent oral intake. Initial evaluation showed no acute findings on labs or chest imaging. ENT evaluation revealed no structural cause, and a video swallow study showed no aspiration but frequent post-swallow coughing likely due to hypersensitivity. A barium swallow revealed moderate esophageal dysmotility, a new finding. She was advanced to a regular diet with improved symptoms using swallowing techniques involving trach occlusion. Pain was controlled with acetaminophen and ibuprofen. Hyperglycemia was noted with an A1c of 7.9, prompting outpatient follow-up. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to see ENT, gastroenterology, and her primary care provider for diabetes evaluation.
